req.title: Reject negative squadNumber
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 422 when squadNumber is not a positive integer.

doc.reasoning: R-PLAYER-023 requires HTTP 422 when squadNumber is not a positive integer. The PlayerRequestModel defines squad_number as int with no explicit gt=0 validator in the source, but the requirement mandates rejection of negative values. Tests cover: (1) positive case — a valid positive squadNumber yields 201; (2) negative case — a negative squadNumber yields 422; (3) boundary case — squadNumber=0 yields 422 (zero is not a positive integer); (4) boundary case — squadNumber=-1 (one below zero boundary) yields 422; (5) boundary case — squadNumber=1 (minimum positive, already in DB so 409, confirming it passes validation) to distinguish validation from conflict. We also test squadNumber=27 (a new positive integer not in DB) to confirm 201, and squadNumber=-999 (deeply negative) to confirm 422. Mutation resilience: exact status code assertions (422 vs 201 vs 409), both sides of the positive-integer boundary (0, -1, 1, positive), catching operator-flip mutations on the validation threshold.

tests.name: test_positive_squad_number_accepted
preconditions: App is running in-process via TestClient
squadNumber=27 does not exist in the pre-loaded database
actions: POST /players/ with a valid payload where squadNumber=27 (a positive integer not in DB)
trace: R-PLAYER-023: positive integer squadNumber must be accepted
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app)

def test_positive_squad_number_accepted():
    payload = {
        "firstName": "Test",
        "lastName": "Player",
        "squadNumber": 27,
        "position": "Goalkeeper"
    }
    r = client.post("/players/", json=payload)
    assert r.status_code == 201
    body = r.json()
    assert body["squadNumber"] == 27
    assert body["firstName"] == "Test"
    assert body["lastName"] == "Player"
